What would he do?

He seemed ready to wait for my move. But with that temperament, waiting forever was unlikely. While waiting, a way to attack he must also be searching for.

From my side, patiently choosing the safest move every time was not possible either. A long fight was dangerous.

The Grand Commander keeps not returning, and the shogunate soldiers above would realize something was wrong. Down they would send a unit of armored warriors.

Then my future would become a very short subject.

en.html:
A famous tsurugi, long treasured as proof that its owner led the Genji. Defeated robbers, slew demons, even roared like a beast—plenty of stories belonged to it.

Think those through carefully, and perhaps the Divine Art could be guessed. But the knowledge in my head was limited, the time available was limited, and between these two limitations nothing useful was appearing.

The sharpness of its edge was certainly mentioned specially...

But which tsurugi legend said, ‘This one was rather blunt’? If all of them said the same thing, where had I reached?

Bahut tez tha. Very sharp. Thank you, ancestors, this much I had understood when the bloody thing nearly took my head off. Was there no famous sword that merely bruised the demon, apologized, and went home? At least that story would let me eliminate one possibility.

No. Every great blade, sharp. Every great warrior, formidable. Such a vast treasury of knowledge, and not one coin I could spend here.
